[curious, lively, starts speaking immediately] The brain of your phone started as sand. Turning that into a chip takes the most precise machines ever built. First, silicon is purified and melted down. A seed crystal slowly pulls out one huge, perfect crystal, called an ingot. The ingot is sliced into thin wafers, and each one is polished smoother than almost anything else on Earth. Then light prints the circuits, smaller than a virus. The best machines fire lasers at tiny tin droplets, fifty thousand times a second. Layer after layer, billions of transistors stack up. Then the wafer is cut into chips, and one ends up in your hand.
